faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your annual gross pay before tax and super. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour yields $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 per year. Remember that super is paid on top of this amount, not deducted from it.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include casual loading?
faqs.a: Yes. On the timesheet page, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading to your base hourly rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, the calculator will apply the loading to show $33.05 per hour. Casual loading is an additional payment to compensate for the lack of paid leave entitlements, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

faqs.q: How is tax and super calculated in the estimate?
faqs.a: Tax uses the 2026–27 resident rates: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy of 2% is added (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). Super is estimated at 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. These are estimates only; your actual tax and super may vary.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you’re negotiating a salary or planning your budget, converting an hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. The standard approach in Australia is to multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees, the assumed week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you a gross annual salary before tax, super, and other deductions.

### The 38-Hour Week and the 52-Week Year

Australia’s full-time standard is 38 hours per week, though some awards or agreements may differ. When using [the timesheet](/) on this site, you can enter your actual weekly hours, but for a standard conversion we assume 38 hours. The formula is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, if you earn the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), your annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44. If you work 40 hours, you would use 40 instead of 38, but note that penalty rates or overtime may apply beyond 38 hours.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Reference

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the minimum wage example: weekly pay = $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72, so fortnightly = $2,009.44. This can help you compare with salary offers that are quoted per fortnight.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

It’s important to know the difference between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and casual loading. The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. However, many industries have award rates that are higher. For example, the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page details these rates.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The casual minimum wage is therefore $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using the calculator, you can check the casual loading box to automatically add this 25%. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your salary. For example, on a $52,269.44 annual salary, your employer would contribute an additional $6,272.33 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your total remuneration (salary plus super) is higher than your gross pay. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay is your gross salary minus tax and the Medicare levy. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% for each dollar over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% for each dollar over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% for each dollar over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% for each dollar over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides a detailed breakdown.

### Using the Novated Lease Take Home Pay Calculator

Our novated lease take home pay calculator helps you estimate your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay after tax and super. It uses the same formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. You can adjust hours if you work part-time or overtime. The calculator also shows the impact of casual loading and provides a tax estimate based on the current rates. This is especially useful if you are considering a novated lease, as your take-home pay affects your ability to make lease payments.

Remember, the calculator is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

### Average Weekly Earnings and Industry Benchmarks

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week as of May 2026. This is an average, not a median for any specific job. If you are comparing your pay to industry averages, note that the ABS figure includes all full-time employees across all industries. For specific award rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) on this site.

### Practical Example: From Hourly to Annual

Let’s say you are a casual worker earning $30.00 per hour (base rate). With casual loading, your effective hourly rate becomes $37.50. For a 38-hour week, your weekly gross is $1,425.00, annual gross is $74,100.00. After tax (using 2026–27 rates) and Medicare, your estimated annual take-home is around $56,000 (depending on your exact circumstances). Your employer would also contribute $8,892.00 in super (12% of $74,100).

This estimate can help you decide if a salary offer is competitive or if a novated lease is affordable. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page offers more examples.

### Important Disclaimer

This calculator and the information provided are for general guidance only. They are not a determination of your actual pay or tax. Always consult a qualified professional for personal financial advice. The figures used are based on publicly available data from the Fair Work Ombudsman, Fair Work Commission, Australian Bureau of Statistics, and Australian Taxation Office.

### Summary

Converting hourly to annual pay is straightforward: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a 38-hour week, this gives a standard full-time annual gross. Remember to add casual loading if applicable, and know that super is paid on top. Use our novated lease take home pay calculator to see your estimated take-home pay and plan your finances with confidence.
